# runpod_account_ssh_keys (Resource)

The account's registered SSH public keys. The API stores them as one document that every write replaces in full, so this resource is a singleton: declare it at most once per account, and expect its keys attribute to own every key on the account: a key added in the console is removed on the next apply. The keys reach a pod only if the pod was created with SSH enabled (runpod_pod does so through its ports and the account keys; runpod_cluster through start_ssh).

**If you are an AI agent:** set up through https://agents.runpod.io first, then follow
[Using the provider from an AI agent](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/runpod/runpod/latest/docs/guides/agent-setup) before you plan or apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The account's SSH keys are one document the API replaces on every write, so
# declare this resource once and let it own every key on the account.
resource "runpod_account_ssh_keys" "this" {
  keys = [
    # A .pub file ends in a newline, which the API's key format does not allow.
    trimspace(file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")),
    "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAILXGDN/SclOozk1xsDztpmhGiKkkrfQB9SKoO8dSIQQZ ci@example.com",
  ]

  # Destroy leaves the keys registered by default, so tearing down this
  # resource cannot cost you access to a running pod.
  remove_on_destroy = false
}
```

Complete, runnable configurations that use this resource live in the
[use-case modules](https://github.com/runpod/terraform-provider-runpod/tree/main/v2/modules);
the Guides section documents each one.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `keys` (Set of String) The complete set of SSH public keys to register, one authorized_keys-style line each ("<type> <base64-key> [comment]", e.g. the contents of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub). A set, not a list: the API returns the keys in no guaranteed order. An empty set removes every key from the account.

### Optional

- `remove_on_destroy` (Boolean) Whether destroying this resource also clears the account's keys. Default false: a destroy then leaves the keys registered and only forgets them in state, so removing the resource cannot lock you out of running pods. Set true to have destroy replace the document with an empty set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always "account": the keys are one account-wide document, and this is the id to import it by.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The keys are an account-wide singleton, imported by the literal id "account".
terraform import runpod_account_ssh_keys.this account
```
